10.1002_adfm.77092: In the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), the optimization of hydrogen binding energy (HBE) is generally constrained by the intrinsic trade‐off between water dissociation and hydrogen adsorption. Herein, we propose a dual‐regulation strategy that enables precise modulation of this trade‐off through the synergistic coupling of lattice strain and interfacial electronic rearrangement. We construct a Fe single‐atom dual‐anchored Ru‐based catalyst (Fe SA Ru NP P@NC), in which Fe atoms are simultaneously embedded within Ru nanoparticles, inducing ∼2.8% lattice compression, and anchored on N, P co‐doped carbon via Fe‐N 3 P 1 coordination, thereby forming a Ru NPs/Fe‐N 3 P 1 ‐C Schottky‐like interface. The lattice compression tunes the Ru d‐band center and weakens the overly strong adsorption of H * and OH * , while interfacial charge redistribution compensates for the electronic structure shift induced by lattice strain, enabling precise regulation of the Ru─H interaction. As a result, the catalyst delivers an outstanding HER performance in 1.0 m KOH, requiring only 22 mV overpotential to reach 10 mA cm −2 , significantly outperforming commercial Pt/C (37 mV). Both experimental and theoretical results demonstrate that the synergistic interplay between lattice strain and interfacial charge transfer promotes water polarization and dissociation, while optimizing adsorption energy matching along the reaction pathway, thereby markedly accelerating HER kinetics.
10.1002_adma.202517489: Poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) remains one of the most widely produced polymers globally but poses significant environmental and energetic challenges due to its high chlorine content, low recyclability, and the energy‐intensive nature of both production and disposal. Here, a sustainable electrochemical approach is reported for the dechlorination of PVC and simultaneous synthetic generation of cyclic acetals, precursors for biodegradable polyesters, employing a Cl 2 ‐shuttle reaction onto vinyl ethers. By systematic electrochemical screening and a Design of Experiments (DoE) optimization strategy, high yields of cyclic acetal formation and elevated dechlorination rates of up to 94% for PVC are achieved. The resulting polymer retains its structural integrity and exhibits internal plasticization via covalent recombination with phthalate plasticizer fragments. This shows that beyond chlorine recovery, the process opens up attractive upcycling pathways through tunable thermal properties of partially dechlorinated PVC. Additionally, our method is tolerant to common plastic additives and applicable to real PVC waste streams, highlighting its robustness and industrial potential. The broad scope of accessible cyclic acetals expands the utility of the reported process using PVC as a chlorine source, providing a platform to produce valuable monomer precursors and enabling facilitated access to versatile, biodegradable polyester materials.
10.1002_adma.74720: Ru‐based catalysts are promising cathodes for alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE), yet sluggish water dissociation, overly strong Ru─H adsorption, and durability loss still limit their practical performance. Herein, we construct a controlled M─N─C (M═Fe, Co, Ni) support series for anchoring Ru particles and establish a dual‐regulation strategy that couples interfacial water activation with support‐induced Ru electronic optimization. M─N 4 coordination motifs mainly regulate the near‐surface water environment and promote water‐dissociation kinetics, while the M─N─C supports modulate the electronic structure of Ru through metal‐support interaction. The optimized Ru/Ni─N─C delivers an ultralow overpotential of 9 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and achieves 4000 mA cm −2 at 2.0 V in a practical AEMWE, with an apparent voltage increase rate of 3.1 µV h −1 over 1600 h. In situ Raman and infrared spectroscopies reveal that Ni─N 4 motifs enrich and polarize interfacial K + ‐H 2 O species, facilitating the Volmer step. Theoretical calculations further show that Ni─N 4 lowers the water dissociation barrier to 0.19 eV, while the Ni─N─C support optimizes Ru─H adsorption to −0.07 eV through metal‐support interaction. This work provides mechanistic guidance for designing efficient Ru‐based alkaline HER catalysts by integrating water‐structure regulation with support‐mediated Ru electronic modulation.
10.1002_anie.6160285: Non‐aqueous flow batteries (NAFBs) require membranes with superior organic solvent resistance and high ionic conductivity in organic solvents to endure the corrosive effects inherent in non‐aqueous electrolytes. Herein, we designed a highly organic‐solvent‐resistant imidazolium‐grafted anion‐exchange membrane (AEM) for NAFBs, realizing rapid anion hopping conduction in organic solvents. The membrane exhibited an ultrafast ionic conductivity as high as 2.1 mS cm −1 in DMF‐based electrolyte which was much greater than that of the commercial Celgard membrane (only 0.45 mS·cm −1 ), coupled with exceptional barrier properties evidenced by ultralow active‐species permeability values of 1.6 × 10 −8 cm 2 s −1 for 2,1,3‐benzothiadiazole anolyte and 3.8 × 10 −9 cm 2 s −1 for 10‐methylphenothiazine catholyte, respectively. Moreover, the membrane demonstrated outstanding stability in aggressive organic solvent, achieving an average energy efficiency (EE) over 66.1% for over 330 cycles at 5 mA cm −2 in a NAFB cell test, which far exceeded the commercial Celgard membrane (with only 70 cycles with an average EE of 48.8%). This research presents a strategic advance in next‐generation membrane design for NAFBs with exceptional organic solvent resistance and high ionic conductivity.
10.1021_acscatal.6c04315: In this work, we report a low-temperature chemical looping strategy for the selective nonoxidative dehydrogenation (NODH) of ethane (C2H6) into ethylene (C2H4) using copper-containing zeolites. The combination of in situ Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), and reactor tests shows that MFI and MOR frameworks with isolated Cu(I) sites are capable of ethane NODH to ethylene at temperatures below 615 K with up to 100% ethylene selectivity: the conditions much milder than that of steam cracking or catalytic dehydrogenation. Copper-containing FAU and CHA show very limited ethylene yield. The significant activity of copper-containing zeolites is achieved through C2H4···Cu(I) π-complexation after dehydrogenation, as revealed by in situ FTIR spectroscopy and XAS, which shifts the thermodynamic equilibrium toward the products by separating ethylene from the gas-phase hydrogen and protecting the formed olefin from the side reactions. The complex can be decomposed upon contact with diluted steam, allowing regeneration of active sites without losing any products. Reactor tests show that MFI is the best performing zeolite among all the frameworks with similar Si/Al ratio, while in situ FTIR spectroscopy indicates that the presence of dual-Cu(I) active sites in the MFI framework leads to high low-temperature C2H6 NODH activity. The contribution of distinct Cu(I) sites hosted by the MFI framework in NODH can be precisely controlled upon fine-tuning of the copper weight loading, Si/Al ratio, and dehydrogenation temperature. This work demonstrates that chemical looping dehydrogenation is compatible with a range of copper-containing zeolites and shows promising potential for further optimization of selective and mild dehydrogenation processes since low operating temperatures would potentially simplify reactor design, remove the necessity for a transfer line exchanger, and enable easier process electrification.
